rules: equilibrium temperature is positive in K (absolute temperature)
equilibrium temperature lies between the two initial temperatures (converted to K), within rounding tolerance, since it is a positive-weighted average
if both initial temperatures are given in K, equilibrium is at least min and at most max of them

functions: Compute the equilibrium temperature of two bodies mixed in an isolated system from their masses, specific heats and initial temperatures.
Compute the heat capacity of a body as mass in grams times specific heat in J/(g·K).
Parse a mass given as text with a unit (g, kg, mg, lb) into grams as a Decimal.
Parse a specific heat given as text with a unit (J/(g·°C), J/(g·K), J/(kg·K), kJ/(kg·K), cal/(g·°C)) into J/(g·K) as a Decimal.
Parse a temperature given as text with a unit (K, °C, °F) into kelvin as a Decimal, applying the proper offset.
Solve the energy balance for the final temperature as the heat-capacity-weighted average of the initial temperatures.
Verify that the heat gained by the colder body equals the heat lost by the hotter body at the equilibrium temperature.
